ai.summary: MultilineInput tracks desired column index in `stickyColumnRef` for vertical cursor navigation. `calculateNewCursorPosition` in `word-wrap-utils.ts` accepts `desiredIndex` to clamp cursor position against line boundaries. Non-vertical keys reset the sticky column. Affects CLI text input component and word-wrap utility.

eli5.text: When you press the up or down arrow keys while typing on multiple lines, your cursor now stays aligned in the same column instead of jumping to the end of shorter lines above or below. Previously, moving vertically reset your horizontal position each time, making it hard to keep your place when editing indented text like code or lists. Now the system remembers your column and keeps you as close to it as possible when crossing lines of different lengths. This behavior is live today for anyone using the CLI multiline text input.

ai.summary: OSC color query logic in `cli/src/utils/terminal-color-detection.ts` refactored to support multiple query strategies for tmux. `buildOscQuery` replaced by `buildOscQueries` returning array of query strings; `tmuxPassthroughState` added to check `allow-passthrough` setting via `spawnSync`. `queryTerminalOSC` now iterates through deduplicated queries until one succeeds. Fallback detection via `TERM_BACKGROUND` and `COLORFGBG` environment variables added.

eli5.text: If you use the assistant inside tmux, it now tries several different ways to ask your terminal what background color theme it should use, instead of relying on just one method that often failed. It checks whether tmux is configured to let color requests through, sends the request wrapped correctly for tmux (or other multiplexers), and if that still doesn't work it falls back to reading theme hints from your terminal's environment variables. You would notice this as the assistant's colors matching your terminal theme more reliably when running inside tmux, which previously often caused mismatched or default colors.

ai.title: Emit toolcall chunk before parsing in stream-parser
ai.summary: The tool_call event now emits with a pre-generated toolCallId before parseRawToolCall executes in packages/agent-runtime/src/tools/tool-executor.ts. Previously, the event fired only after successful parsing, causing missing history entries when parsing failed. stream-parser.ts propagates the generated toolCallId to both standard and custom tool executors. This ensures consistent tool call tracking in message history regardless of parse outcomes.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to perform an action using a built-in tool, the assistant now records that request in your conversation history before attempting to interpret what the tool needs to do. If the instructions for the tool are malformed or unreadable, that entry still appears in the history, so you can see the assistant tried to act even if it failed to complete the step. This affects only conversations where the assistant invokes tools, and it prevents your message history from silently missing those attempts when parsing errors occur.

Implementation includes `cli/src/components/ask-user/` components for navigation, validation, and progress indicators, plus `useAskUserBridge` hook integration in `cli/src/chat.tsx`. This is live today for the Base2 planning agent, whose instructions now tell it to ask clarifying questions via this form before writing specs, while the general chat interface simply subscribes to display such forms whenever an agent triggers them.

Anthropic claude-sonnet-4.5 removed from active judging. judgeAgents structure changed from array to Record<string, AgentDefinition>, runSingleJudge now accepts judgeAgentId string instead of numeric index. Parallel execution reduced from 3 to 2 judges.

eli5.text: The system that internally checks and grades AI coding attempts now relies on a newer pair of AI models to hand out scores. Instead of three models weighing in, two do the evaluating, and one of the previously used models is no longer involved. If you looked now, you'd only see the two newer models running the checks that used to be split across three.

ai.title: Billing monthly reset uses grantCreditOperation with tx
ai.summary: Monthly reset grant path in `packages/billing/src/grant-credits.ts` now calls `grantCreditOperation` with the active `tx` instead of `processAndGrantCredit`. Ensures free and referral credit grants share the same transaction as the `next_quota_reset` update, preventing idle transaction errors. Scope limited to billing package internal grant logic. Referral bonus path receives identical `tx` propagation.

eli5.text: The system that handles monthly billing resets now processes all credit grants, including free credits and referral bonuses, in a single, unified step tied to the reset update. This prevents errors that could occur when the system tried to grant credits separately from updating your quota reset date. If you were affected by the previous approach, you'll notice the monthly reset now completes more reliably without stalling.

ai.title: CLI abstracts web API details via CodebuffApiClient
ai.summary: New `CodebuffApiClient` abstracts web API interactions, replacing direct `fetch` calls in login, user details, publishing, and referral flows. Refactored hooks and commands now use `getApiClient()` and `setApiClientAuthToken()`, improving error handling and type safety. Covers `cli/src/utils/codebuff-api.ts`, `cli/src/commands/publish.ts`, `cli/src/commands/referral.ts`, and related hooks.

eli5.text: When you use the CLI to log in, publish your agents, or claim a referral bonus, the program now talks to the website through a single, well-behaved helper that bundles up your login token and translates error messages, instead of each command crafting its own request. If a network hiccup happens, the helper can tell a temporary problem from a real failure and retry only when it makes sense, and every part of the CLI shares that one helper so error handling stays consistent. The changes are live today for anyone running the CLI commands that log you in, fetch your account details, publish agents, or redeem referrals, so you may notice friendlier error messages or smoother retries where things used to fail silently, while the behind-the-scenes behavior you see day to day otherwise remains

ai.title: Fix invalid API key error code from 404 to 401
ai.summary: The /api/v1/me endpoint now returns HTTP 401 instead of 404 when an invalid API key is provided. The CLI ReferralBanner component was updated to detect this 401 error and display a specific 'Session expired' message rather than a generic failure. This change affects the web API handler in _get.ts and the CLI UI in referral-banner.tsx.

eli5.text: When you're signed in to the CLI but your login has expired, the tool now correctly tells you 'Session expired' instead of a generic error or a 'not found' message. Previously the system sent back a 404 (which wrongly implies the feature itself doesn't exist), so the CLI couldn’t tell that your session had timed out and just showed a vague failure notice. Now, when the server gets an invalid API key it responds with a 401 Unauthorized status code, a standard signal that the login is no longer valid, and the CLI detects that specific code before showing you the more helpful session-expired guidance. This fix applies to anyone logging in through the command-line tool whose authentication token has lapsed, and the change is already live today.

eli5.text: The usage banner now shows different text and colors based on your credit balance, and it updates automatically when credits change. You'll notice the banner displays whether your balance is loading, shows colored alerts when credits run low, and appears or disappears depending on your remaining credits. This logic was moved behind the scenes to make the banner's code cleaner and more reliable, though what you see on screen stays the same.

ai.title: Fix tab auto-complete when slash menu disabled
ai.summary: CLI chat input now suppresses slash menu keyboard handling when `disableSlashSuggestions` is active. The `useSuggestionMenuHandlers` hook accepts a `disableSlashMenu` prop, derived from `getInputModeConfig(inputMode)`, which early-returns in `handleSlashMenuKey` to prevent tab interference. This ensures the file menu tab handler remains functional when slash suggestions are disabled. Changes are scoped to `cli/src/chat.tsx` and `cli/src/hooks/use-suggestion-menu-handlers.ts`.

eli5.text: In the command-line chat, pressing Tab now opens the file picker menu correctly even when the slash command suggestions are turned off. Previously, when slash suggestions were disabled, the Tab key handler that should open the file menu was being blocked by leftover keyboard logic for that disabled menu, so Tab did nothing. The system now checks whether the slash menu is disabled before deciding whether to intercept Tab, allowing the file menu to appear as expected. This behavior is live today for command-line chat users who have slash suggestions disabled.

ai.title: Max mode editor drops gemini for gpt-5
ai.summary: Max mode editor implementor spawning replaces gemini agents with a fixed opus/gpt-5 pattern. Default mode retains gemini, while max mode now uses a 10-slot MAX_MODEL_PATTERN array in .agents/editor/best-of-n/editor-best-of-n.ts. Default max mode parallel agent count reduces from 6 to 5.

eli5.text: When you use Max mode in the editor, it now uses more GPT-5 and less Gemini compared to before. Previously, Max mode would spawn a mix that included Gemini agents, but now it follows a fixed pattern of Opus and GPT-5 agents. The default mode still uses Gemini as before. This change also slightly reduces how many parallel agents Max mode can spawn at once (from 6 to 5).
